asr.full_text: All right, welcome everyone to the show. My name is Katherine Gu, Head of Product Digital Assets at Solano Foundation. We have this mini-Podcast series around the Solana developer platform. So today, here with me is Dan Motiz from Modern Treasury. Dan, glad to have you here. You know, I'd love to just for you to introduce to our audience like who you are, you know, your journey with respect to maybe even start from Visa Visa Crypto days but be even their Modern Treasurer? And what do you do today at Modern Treasurer? Awesome. Good to see you again. Thank you for having me. Yeah. As Catherine said, my name is Dan Motys. I've known Catherine for a long while now from the days of Visa Crypto. I worked there from roughly 2021 to 2022. I've spent my whole career in money movement, basically. And so I started at Visa, focusing on traditional ways of the card network moving money that often involved no card credential. And my interest evolved into how stablecoins could represent a way through which the card networks could move money more efficiently and globally using the primitive that is a stablecoin and so ultimately worked in that team for a while now which is where as i said i overlapped with catherine um and then um i jumped out in march of 2022 to build a platform called beam beam became what people are calling a stablecoin orchestration platform, which allows for you know, normal businesses. Merchants, PSP's, Enterprises to move value from a bank account into a blockchain in the form of a stablecoin. And then back, and we actually spent a lot of time thinking through what it looked like when you connected Instant Rails in particular into Blockchains, such that effectively the developer, the merchant, whomever was using our services, didn't really need to understand the difference between difference between, like what RTP was or real-time payments or what an onchange transfer on Solana was, for example. So, yeah, it's been a bunch, a bunch of time doing that, work with some awesome companies in the space, a lot of which were built on top of Solana. And then more recently recently I sold my company to Modern Treasury in October of this past year. And we've been—we spent the last four or so months kind of heads down integrating Beam into the Modern Treasury platform. And then about two weeks ago, we relaunched under the kind of MT Flagship logo. And we're now going to be actively working on stablecoin registration use cases with folks as a part of the broader Modern Treasury payments platform. So yeah, that's the quick and dirty of it. AMANDA SANSTHAGIRANDI- That's awesome, and it's super exciting. And I think what's really unique is also the fact that Modern Treasury has been around in the industry for a long time and it's more kind of focused on FinTech and Web 2, but now it's sort of this pivot into stablecoins which is really encouraging. I guess as you were thinking about the role that Modern Treasury plays inside the Sivana developer platform, like give us briefly how you think like Modern Treasury plays the role as part of the infrared partners on the back end. And also what are some of the most relevant use cases that you can envision an institution to build? Definitely. Yeah, so I think as one of the most relevant use cases that you can, you can envision an institution to build? Definitely. Yeah, so I think as it relates to kind of how modern treasury thinks about it, as I said, we relaunched a platform that we called Payments recently. Payments will be a part of the Solana developer platform. But think of Payments as basically two different types of product. First of which is the one we've been kind of actively selling and which Beam was a big part of. Which is a full-stack payment services platform such that we can use our underlying regulated financial infrastructure partners' accounts to move money on our customers behalf or their end customer's behalf. So this is something that the likes of Stripe and others in market have been doing for a long while. Historically, Modern Treasury actually did not do that, but we decided that that's part of the ecosystem that we wanted to play a role in. In particular, as it relates to my work, we believe that there's still a lot of room for great capabilities to allow for it to be a lot more simple for normal businesses and traditional market participants to move money into an out of blockchain. Point being, you know, you could be an enterprise, you could be a bank, you could be a corporate and you could use this API to very quickly, very rapidly get money onto Salana. However, where Modern Treasury started was actually a little bit different than that. They actually started in a model where basically folks would bring their own bank account and then modern treasury was a SAS platform that sat on top of various banks in the United States that made the instruction of those banks to move money much easier and the reporting for that money movement much easier, so I think as it relates to kind of the evolution of the platform and as it relates to folks that may be listening to this as a part of the broader Solana Developer Platform initiative, I think the most interesting thing to me is that you could start using Solana Developer Platform in modern treasury, under the hood with the PSP model and get going really quickly in a world where we manage a lot of the underlying complexity of connecting into Solana and connecting into crypto liquidity and connecting into fiat liquidity and connecting into the fiat rails themselves connecting in to the fiat rails themselves. But if and when you graduate or perhaps you already have dozens of bank accounts around the world, the same kind of API layer that we have is connected into a lot of the banks around the world and can actually still be relevant when it is time for you to actually use your own underlying financial infrastructure. So we kind of think of it as is this forever payments platform concept. And so, you know, start now it does, we grow together. And then if you graduate to your own banks, you don't have to refactor your entire platform with a new API build. And to what we're discussing, and what we're working on with the salon developer platform, effectively, that model will be available to folks that build on top of a salon developer platform. Yeah, I think that's a really great point. That way, that model will be available to folks that build on top of a Solana developer platform. That's a really great point. I think the key is really having that agility in terms of the implementation and that developer experience. What does that look like on day one? But also as you're graduating towards the full-on version, how can we help on the backend? I really liked that. I guess, as you guys, again focus everything about Stable stablecoin, stablecoin orchestration and evaluating between different chains. What do you think stands out the most about Solana? And as you know, that right now, one of our key use cases already on the chain is around payments. So why and how do you think we will keep on winning? I would say… Yeah, yeah. I mean, I think payments are in vogue now, but many people have been working hard to crack payments for a long while. And so Catherine, to your point, like payments are a proven use case on the Solana blockchain and in working with customers that have a whole host of different chain options, we've had folks come to us and say that we want to go with Solana and if you can support that great, we'll work with you, if not, maybe it doesn't make sense. And so I think the chain the way, you know, based on the way the chain was built, obviously there's plenty of other use cases that it can solve for, but it was purpose built to solve for things like payments. And yeah, I mean, it's withstood the test of time already. I'm proving itself out as critical infrastructure that can support like real adoption of payments as money moves on chain, which is just beginning to get tested in our nest. Right. So I think that's probably the first I think secondly or, like, real adoption of payments as money moves onChain, which is just beginning to get tested in our Nest, right? So I think that's probably the first though. I think, secondly, I'm super, super impressed over time with the Solana team. They've been immensely supportive of myself and the being journey myself when I was still at Visa, and also now, you know, the work that we're doing at Modern Treasury. I think Solana was, like, the groups that we're doing at Modern Treasury, I think Solana was one of the groups that cracked the code around building a business development cohort around the chain and has succeeded because of that and has built an amazing community around the blockchain itself. And one of the reasons I'm particularly excited about Solana Developer Platform is that now there's this community, these advocates are all around the world for this chain, there's this usage, these advocates all around the world for this chain, there's this usage of this chain and the developer platform is a way through which more people can more simply use it. So it's definitely filling a gap in the broader stack in Solana land, if you will. Absolutely I think that's a great point and I do think the reason why as a foundation we're creating the SDP is more like this is a piece of public infrastructure if you will, right? But the point is to like this is. Piece of public infrastructure as you will. Right. But the point is to really spotlight all the best ecosystem partners, because that's the thing we have, which is the most valuable assets. Uh, being the partners and the developers on this ecosystem. So, uh, wanting to do as much as we could together with you guys, you know, as being design partners, you really paved the way out. Um, I guess my last question is kind of coming back to the core of money movement, right? Because you're really the expert guru in all of these, both coming from a TradFi experience, but also as you're building a lot of these orchestrations. I think one thing is what is the sort of the friction point as of today in the existing money movement that we're still trying to solve? Because frankly, Visa Direct and the likes are doing pretty good job in terms of making money move 24-7 and stuff like that. And my second question is also, do you think stablecoin orchestration can solve for all the existing problems? And given so many competitors are in the space, it's increasing becoming commoditized. So what would be the competitive edges that, from a modern treasury perspective, you want to showcase? And ideally, that can also be realized and built out in the iterations of the SDP. Definitely. Yeah, I think there's plenty of really interesting solutions in fiat land and in market to solve... To make the money movement better broadly. VisaDirect is one example. MasterCard has a product called MasterCard Move that does a lot of similar stuff and more in some cases. There's domestic real-time payment systems in the US and Singapore and India and Brazil a lot of which are talked about broadly in the payments sphere. I think kind of, thing one is that they're outside of Visa and MasterCard really there's not any global, you know, bringing inverse settlement engine that connects various disparate domestic systems around the world. So, um, Visa is an example of a way through which you can solve that. Swift is another example of a way through which you can solve that, but both of them haven't yet cracked how to make settlement and liquidity management more effective and so I personally find myself kind of always harking, you know, coming back to the fact that on-chain money movement and on-chain liquidity, in some cases, which is a stablecoin, in other cases, maybe there's some tokenized asset that somebody cooks up in the next couple of years that we haven't even thought of yet, but on-chain liquidity is a superior form of liquidity because it's readily available around the world at any time. Um, so long as there's an internet connection and so long as obviously, you've done things from a compliance perspective, get access to it. Um, and that hadn't existed before blockchains. And I think that is, in my opinion, the most interesting thing about stablecoins and what's possible here, and something that is not yet solved by really any fintech in the world. So, personally, that's one I'm really excited to kind of like, see come to fruition as this next wave of innovation happens, and this next wave of builders come into the ecosystem using things like the digital platform and modern treasury stack. And I guess the other thing that I'd say is like there's still plenty of places even in the domestic context that just don't quite have infrastructure that, you know, that was that is kind of on par with some of the infrastructure that's been built out in more uh developed jurisdictions and so i think that one's talked more frequently but definitely a believer that you know on-chain financial services broadly are super compelling for places that may have an internet connection but they may not have like a domestic clearing network that's super advanced like what exists in other more established financial markets yeah that's a really good point i guess trying to to connect the internet money with the internet capital markets and everything together, based on Wi-Fi hopefully. We'll see. Super exciting. So, thank you so much, Dan, for being here, and we really look forward to working with you guys in the future through SDP and VR. Likewise, likewise, thank you. Thank you.
